items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Have you heard of some of the other drummers coming up, like El Negro Hernandez from Cuba? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah. He’s a fantastic drummer.

ctx.x: That’s right. Tony Williams was a baby. That’s right. Steve Gadd, same way. Buddy Rich was known as “Traps.” He told me – he said he didn’t have any idea of becoming a drummer when he was little. He played in the circuit in the theaters, but he wasn’t interested in pursuing it, becoming a full-fledged drummer. It just happened.
Have you heard of some of the other drummers coming up, like El Negro Hernandez from Cuba?

Oh yeah. He’s a fantastic drummer. Man. Talking about being mad at somebody. I’m going to break his hands. Because to me, those guys are a full rhythm section within themselves. It used to be, I played the samba and things like that, I had three other guys helping me. Now these guys play a clavé beat with the left foot, and the right foot’s doing something different, and the other hand – he’s fantastic.
